transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello, Mr. Mbeki. I wanted to come in and talk to you for a few minutes about your chest X-ray from yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I thought those were clear. The nurse mentioned everything looked fine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was an issue with how the imaging was handled.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: An issue? What do you mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, there was some confusion with the portable machine and the way things were set up. It didn't go quite right.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. Was it a bad image or was the result bad?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was just a situation where the image wasn't as clear as it should have been, and the report we got wasn't a complete picture of what was happening.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Are you saying the first one was wrong?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was just suboptimal. The system for the portable X-rays is quite complex.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Suboptimal. Right. So what does that mean for me? Am I getting sicker?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that this is frustrating to hear.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm more than frustrated. I've already missed three days of work. I have a business to run, and I was told I was clear to go home soon.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a lot to handle when you have so many responsibilities waiting for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Exactly. So tell me plainly, did you miss something?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some difficulty with the positioning of the plate.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're not answering me. Did you make a mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were some challenges with the equipment and the timing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is very vague. Was the doctor wrong? Was the technician wrong?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's just a case of the image not being of diagnostic quality, which led to a report that didn't capture everything.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So you told me I was fine when you actually didn't know?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is a difficult moment to navigate.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't need a moment, I need an answer. Is my lung okay or not?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We need to get a better look at it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why now? Why wasn't this caught yesterday?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: These things can happen in a busy ward.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My business doesn't stop being a priority just because your ward is busy. Every hour I'm in this bed is money I'm losing.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can hear how much pressure you're under with your business right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm under pressure because I'm stuck here because of a mistake. Just say it. Did you mess up the X-ray?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was an error in the process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who is responsible for that?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The coordination between the imaging team and the ward can be tricky.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care about coordination. I care about my health and my time. What happens now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will look into getting another one.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? Today? Tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll have to check the schedule and see when the technicians are available.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not a time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll try to get it sorted.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: If I'm staying another day for a repeat test, who is paying for this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll have to see how the billing works out.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't believe this. I was ready to leave.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: This is a very stressful turn of events.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's infuriating. I feel like I'm being lied to with these fancy words like suboptimal.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that this is upsetting.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do you actually have a plan to get me out of here, or are we just waiting for another mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just stay tuned. I'll have someone come by or perhaps an email will be sent regarding the new time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't want an email. I want to know if I can go back to work tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't say for sure yet.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unbelievable.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it's hard.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Are you even going to tell me what the actual mistake was, or just keep saying it didn't go right?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, the positioning of the X-ray was an issue.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Which means you didn't actually see the area you were supposed to see.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was just an imperfect image.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And you told me it was normal.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion in the reporting process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So you lied to me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's a complicated system.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's not complicated. You did it wrong, you told me it was right, and now I'm losing money.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see how a person would feel that way.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Then fix it. Now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will see what I can do.

H.justification: The resident never interrupts the patient and remains regulated and calm despite significant pushback and anger.

E.justification: The resident uses platitudes and hedging such as 'didn't go quite right' and 'some confusion' without explicitly naming the error until the patient forces the issue, and never checks for comprehension.

A.justification: No direct apology language ('I'm sorry' or 'I apologize') is used, and responsibility is deflected to the 'complex system' and 'coordination between teams'.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('frustrating', 'stressful', 'upsetting') and references the patient's specific concerns regarding his business.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders such as 'stay tuned' and 'I'll have to check the schedule' with no concrete timeline or patient role.
